label: COFEPRIS
description: Federal commission for protection against health risks. Regulates human medicines and controlled substances, including psychotropics scheduled under the General Health Law.

label: SENASICA
description: Agriculture-sector agency that registers and authorizes chemical, pharmaceutical and biological products for animal use.
source: Gobierno de México, “Regulación de productos veterinarios”

label: LGS art. 245, group II
description: Pentobarbital is listed among group II psychotropics: substances with “some therapeutic value” that “constitute a serious problem for public health.” A veterinary product and a scheduled psychotropic at once.
verification_note: Next step: establish which prescription and dispensing rules apply when a group II substance is sold through veterinary channels.
source: Ley General de Salud, art. 245, fracción II

label: NOM-033-SAG/ZOO-2014
description: Official Mexican standard on methods for killing domestic and wild animals. The likely normative frame for veterinary euthanasia.
source: Diario Oficial de la Federación, NOM-033-SAG/ZOO-2014

label: General Health Law, palliative care title (Título Octavo Bis)
description: Federal law. Its palliative-care title (arts. 166 Bis to 166 Bis 21) obliges doctors to respect a terminally ill patient's decisions about treatment and forbids extraordinary measures without consent. Art. 166 Bis 21 prohibits euthanasia, defined as homicide out of pity, and assisted suicide, referring to the Federal Penal Code. Distinct from the state Voluntad Anticipada laws.
source: Ley General de Salud, arts. 166 Bis 15, 166 Bis 17, 166 Bis 21

label: Advance-directive laws (Voluntad Anticipada)
description: State laws that let a person record in advance their refusal of life-prolonging treatment. Mexico City was first, in January 2008; Puebla joined in July 2024. As of July 2024, 15 states had one (not Jalisco or Baja California). They govern withdrawal of treatment, not euthanasia.
verification_note: Recount if citing a current number.
source: Ley de Voluntad Anticipada: El derecho a una muerte digna; TV Azteca (July 2024) for the state list

label: “Life from conception” state provisions
description: State constitutional protections of life “from conception to natural death.” Often read as obstacles to assisted-dying legislation.
verification_note: Their legal effect on end-of-life law needs state-by-state analysis. Do not describe them as a categorical block.
source: Secondary sources; state constitutions to consult

label: US federal case, N.D. Illinois
description: Indicted in May 2024 for importing pentobarbital from Mexico and selling it online. Guilty plea in February 2025 to one count of importing a controlled substance. The release says the drug is sold in Mexico to euthanize animals.
verification_note: Documents particular conduct, not the scale or organization of a market. Sentencing outcome still to check.

label: Veterinary euthanasia practice
description: Clinics and practitioners for whom killing with pentobarbital is routine, legitimate and professionally governed. The hinge of the subproject: where a “good death” is most ordinary.
verification_note: To be documented through interviews and observation.

label: Veterinary pharmaceutical distribution
description: Distributors, agricultural and veterinary supply stores. The grant describes over-the-counter markets as MORTALMED's Mexico site.
verification_note: How the group II scheduling works in these channels in practice is an open empirical question.

label: Veterinary formulations
description: Concentration, labelling, packaging and dosing designed for animal bodies and clinical settings. What stays materially continuous when the product leaves that frame?
verification_note: Document from product registrations and package inserts, not from user accounts.

label: INCan, Mexico City
description: National Cancer Institute. Fieldsite of a recent ethnography of palliative care and end-of-life choice.

label: Palliative care clinicians
description: Clinicians who widen patient choice on paper while often opposing assisted dying. They show what remains unimaginable within legitimate care.

label: AVMA (US)
description: US veterinary association that has flagged cross-border movement of veterinary pentobarbital as illegal.

label: Right-to-die advocacy and information
description: Narratives that frame Mexican veterinary pentobarbital as “the Mexico option.” Informational circulation: the drug becomes consequential far away, whether or not anything moves.
verification_note: Trace through published advocacy texts and their reception.
source: Advocacy literature; trade and wire press

label: Catholic Church and allied opposition
description: Main institutional opponent of assisted-dying legalization. A 2008 poll is often cited for 59% public support of physician-assisted death.
verification_note: Find the original poll and current public statements. Current source is secondary.

label: Trade and wire press
description: Veterinary trade press and wire journalism documenting cross-border pentobarbital stories since the 2000s. A source of the border frame the subproject should not adopt as its headline.

label: MORTALMED
description: ERC Starting Grant (PI Marcos Freire de Andrade Neves, University of Glasgow, 2026–2031). Sodium pentobarbital as pharmakon; necro-sociality across Switzerland, the US and Mexico.

label: Van der Geest, Whyte & Hardon 1996
description: “The Anthropology of Pharmaceuticals: A Biographical Approach.” Following drugs through production, marketing, distribution, prescription, consumption and efficacy.

label: Hardon & Sanabria 2017
description: “Fluid Drugs: Revisiting the Anthropology of Pharmaceuticals.” Drug effects and identities emerge through changing relations among labs, markets, regulators and care. Moves beyond a linear life cycle.

label: Mol 2002
description: The Body Multiple: Ontology in Medical Practice. One object, enacted differently in different practices, and coordinated (or not).

label: Appadurai (ed.) 1986, incl. Kopytoff
description: The Social Life of Things; Kopytoff on the cultural biography of things. How objects gain and lose statuses as they move.

label: Law 2004
description: After Method: Mess in Social Science Research. Realities assembled through heterogeneous relations.

label: Hayden 2023
description: The Spectacular Generic: Pharmaceuticals and the Simipolitical in Mexico. The Mexican pharmacy and generic drugs as public, political terrain.

label: Singer & Ordóñez Vázquez 2025
description: “A Time to Die: Mexican Life Debates and the Paradox of Choice in Palliative Care.” A year of fieldwork at INCan.

label: Morris 2012
description: Blue Juice: Euthanasia in Veterinary Medicine. Ethnography of veterinary killing, named after pentobarbital solution.

label: Sanders 1995
description: “Killing with Kindness: Veterinary Euthanasia and the Social Construction of Personhood.”

label: Haraway 2008
description: When Species Meet. On killing well, sharing suffering and responsibility in multispecies relations.

label: Orrego, “Mapping Unwanted Relatedness”
description: Care enacted as lethal maintenance in human-rat relations in Medellín. A multispecies route into licensed killing.

label: Orrego, “It All Depends on the Amount”
description: Ethnography of Bogotá's Samper Mendoza herb market (27 visits, 2025). Potency as relational, not intrinsic: the same substance is remedy or poison depending on dose, preparation and protocol. Shows the counter as a situated clinic where sellers read requests and decide, printed labels and spoken corrections as competing regimes of evidence, and an ethics of not reproducing risky instructions.
verification_note: Update the status line once the manuscript is under review.

label: Buchbinder 2021
description: Scripting Death: Stories of Assisted Dying in America. How medical aid in dying is scripted in practice.

label: Gandsman 2018
description: “Old age is cruel”: The right to die as an ethics for living. On right-to-die activism, where the right to die is framed as an ethics for how to live in old age. Bears directly on informational circulation.
source: Gandsman (2018), “Old age is cruel”: The right to die as an ethics for living

label: Hull 2012
description: Government of Paper: The Materiality of Bureaucracy in Urban Pakistan. Documents as things that make objects and authority.

label: Riley (Erasmus MC)
description: How restricting lethal drugs pushes assisted dying and executions toward compounded or unregulated alternatives.
source: Oregon Health Authority, Death with Dignity Act

label: ANAM (Mexican customs)
description: Agencia Nacional de Aduanas de México, the customs agency created in 2022. Where a veterinary product leaving the country becomes a matter of export control and inspection.

label: US Customs and Border Protection
description: The US border agency. On the US side of the border, the same product stops being a veterinary medicine and becomes a controlled substance subject to seizure.

label: Special prescription regime for group II psychotropics
description: Group II psychotropics are dispensed under a special prescription system. The key question for the subproject is how this works when the buyer is a veterinarian and the patient an animal: who can prescribe, and what is recorded.
verification_note: Locate the exact articles of the Ley General de Salud and its regulations on prescription, and any veterinary-specific rules.
source: Ley General de Salud (articles to confirm)

label: Couriers and postal channels
description: The ordinary logistics through which goods cross borders. Recorded only as a category: how parcels are declared, inspected and seized, never specific services or routes.
source: Category; documented through court and customs records

label: Informal resale
description: Sale outside authorized veterinary channels. Recorded only as a category, at the level of how it works and how it is talked about and policed, never with sellers, places or prices.
verification_note: To be documented through interviews, court records and regulatory alerts, within the ethics protocol.

label: Intermediaries
description: People who connect supply and demand across jurisdictions. Recorded only as a role, through public documents such as indictments, never as identifiable individuals.
verification_note: Document through court records and press, within the ethics protocol.
source: Category; US Attorney's Office records and press

label: Online marketplaces and forums
description: Where information, claims about availability and offers circulate. Studied as informational circulation: what is said, believed and warned against, never as a directory.
verification_note: Define sampling and ethics for online research before any data collection.

label: People seeking access
description: Foreign and Mexican people who look for the drug to end their lives, and those close to them. Approached through published accounts, advocacy material and, if ethically approved, interviews; never identified.
verification_note: Requires a specific ethics protocol, including safeguarding and referral to support services.

label: Shapiro & Kirksey 2017
description: “Chemo-Ethnography: An Introduction.” Ethnography that follows chemicals and their effects through bodies, environments and institutions. A methodological anchor for following pentobarbital as a substance.

label: Ong & Collier (eds.) 2005
description: Global Assemblages: Technology, Politics, and Ethics as Anthropological Problems. A reference point for assemblage ethnography.
